hpi: {{patient_name}} is a 29-year-old who presents with alternating diarrhea and constipation, abdominal pain relieved by defecation, and bloating — meeting Rome IV criteria for IBS (recurrent abdominal pain + ≥2 of: improvement with defecation, change in stool frequency, change in stool appearance). ESR and CRP are normal, ruling out inflammatory bowel disease. Stool studies are negative for infectious etiology. IBS is a diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out celiac disease (anti-tTG, anti-endomysial antibodies), C. difficile, parasites, and colorectal cancer. Conservative management is key: high-fiber diet, lactose-free trial, exercise, trigger food avoidance. Loperamide PRN for diarrhea, antispasmodics (dicyclomine/hyoscyamine) PRN. Colonoscopy/sigmoidoscopy is NOT appropriate — invasive testing loses points in stable patients with normal screening labs. TCA/SSRI for refractory cases at follow-up.
